sentences.text: Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro (; born 30 April 1981) is a Brazilian lawyer and conservative politician serving as a senator for Rio de Janeiro since 2019.
A son of the 38th president of Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro, he is affiliated with the Liberal Party (PL).
He previously served as a state deputy of Rio de Janeiro from 2003 to 2019.
As a state deputy, Bolsonaro held the presidency of the Special Committee on Family Planning.
His political career culminated in his election to the Senate in 2018, where he garnered 4.38 million votes.

His political career has been closely associated with his father and has included controversial positions on Brazil's military dictatorship, criminal justice, and the death penalty, as well as involvement in the Rachadinhas corruption investigation, a scheme to embezzle some of the salaries of parliamentary advisors.

He is also being investigated in connection with the Banco Master scandal, due to an alleged transaction of 134 million reais related to former banker Daniel Vorcaro and the financing of the film Dark Horse, which was to portray the life of Jair Bolsonaro, leading to an investigation by the Federal Police (PF) on suspicion of money laundering, corruption, and tax evasion.

Bolsonaro was the PL candidate in the 2026 presidential election with the endorsement of his father, losing to incumbent president (and Jair's 2022 opponent) Lula da Silva in the second round after placing first in the first round.
He is the first Brazilian presidential candidate to place first in the first round but lose in the second round.

After losing the election, he did not accept the results, fled to the United States with the help of a former Mossad agent and in a private jet whose owner has ties to individuals convicted in the US for money laundering and narcotrafficking, and proclaimed himself the "true president-elect"; however, his own party, world leaders, and Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) recognized Lula's victory.
Later, Bolsonaro changed the wording to "leader" following an order by the US government.
He is currently under criminal investigation in Brazil.
Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro was born in Resende, Rio de Janeiro, at the Military Academy of Agulhas Negras, to Jair Bolsonaro and Rogéria Nantes Braga.
He graduated from Candido Mendes University with a bachelor of laws degree.
During his time at university, he was also officially employed in a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position at the leadership office of the PPB party in the Chamber of Deputies in Brasília.

Reporting by BBC Brasil later highlighted a conflict between his official employment in Brasília and his simultaneous in-person attendance at law school and at a volunteer internship at the Public Defender's Office in Rio de Janeiro.
He holds specializations in public policy from the University Research Institute of Rio de Janeiro and in entrepreneurship from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation.
Bolsonaro was elected to his first term in the 2002 Brazilian general election.
He was re-elected as a state deputy in 2006, 2010, and in his last candidacy, in 2014, for the 2015–2019 period.
In April 2015, he voted in favor of the appointment of Domingos Brazão to the Rio de Janeiro State Court of Accounts.
Brazão would later be accused of being behind the 2018 assassination of Rio de Janeiro city councillor and political activist Marielle Franco (1979–2018).
On 12 April 2016, Bolsonaro and his bodyguard, who is also a military police officer, exchanged gunfire with two robbers who were holding up a car ahead of them in Rio de Janeiro's West Zone.
One of the assailants was injured and fled on a motorcycle.
Like other members of the Bolsonaro family, he opposes what he calls "the media exploitation of human rights enforcement for the benefit of crime and criminals."

In December 2018, the newspaper O Estado de S. Paulo revealed that a report from the Council for Financial Activities Control (COAF) had identified an atypical movement of R$ 1.2 million in an account in the name of Fabrício Queiroz, a former aide to Bolsonaro.
This marked the beginning of the "rachadinhas case" and led the Rio de Janeiro Public Prosecutor's Office to open an investigation that lasted two years.
The probe resulted in charges for the crimes of fraud, embezzlement, money laundering, and criminal organization being filed against Bolsonaro, Queiroz, and 15 other individuals involved.
In 2021, the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) annulled the previous rulings on the case involving Queiroz and Bolsonaro.
The evidence obtained by breaking the banking, tax, and telephone secrecy of the investigated parties—which had been used to support the Public Prosecutor's charges—was invalidated.

In the 2018 elections, Bolsonaro ran for Senator from the state of Rio de Janeiro for the Social Liberal Party (PSL).
The then state deputy's candidacy was announced at the PSL's national convention, held on 22 July 2018, in a convention center in Rio de Janeiro.
At the same event, the Jair Bolsonaro 2018 presidential campaign was formalized.
In the election, Bolsonaro received 4,380,418 votes (31.36% of the total valid votes), being elected for the 56th legislature (2019–2027) of the Brazilian Federal Senate.
On 6 February 2019, he was elected 3rd Secretary of the Senate's board of directors.

On 11 June 2019, President Jair Bolsonaro awarded him the medal of the Order of Naval Merit during a ceremony commemorating the Battle of Riachuelo at the Brasília Marine Corps Group, located on the shores of Lake Paranoá.

On 5 December 2025, Bolsonaro publicly announced his candidacy for president in the 2026 Brazilian general election, stating he had received the nomination from his father during a visit to the prison where the latter is being held at the Federal Police headquarters in Brasília.

In a statement released on his social media, the senator declared: "It is with great responsibility that I confirm the decision of Brazil's greatest political and moral leader, Jair Messias Bolsonaro, to entrust me with the mission of continuing our national project."

The decision was communicated beforehand to the Liberal Party (PL) and the governor of São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, who until then was the main candidate expected to be Jair Bolsonaro's choice in the elections, signaling that he would run for the presidency while Tarcísio is likely to focus on reelection.

The announcement generated positive reactions among his allies, including federal congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL), who expressed support for his brother, and the national president of the PL, Valdemar Costa Neto, who endorsed the choice.
Bolsonaro's candidacy was supported internationally by Argentine President Javier Milei, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, and American President Donald Trump.
According to sitting environment minister Marina Silva, think tank Chatham House, and others, a Bolsonaro victory would have put the Amazon rainforest at risk.
His presidential campaign placed particular emphasis on public security and crime policy.
He was one of the two leading presidential candidates going into the first round of voting on 4 October.

Shortly before the final debate hosted by TV Globo, he withdrew from it, citing a decision by a justice of the Superior Electoral Court that prohibited the placement of an empty lectern bearing Lula’s name.
Bolsonaro won a plurality of 47% of the vote over incumbent president Lula da Silva's 45% in the election on 4 October.
He then lost the election in the following runoff vote on 25 October.
Lula da Silva took 51.8% of the vote and Bolsonaro took 48.2%.
Immediately following the vote, Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek to have the vote annulled.
However, he later conceded that Lula won the election.

After his loss, the Supreme Federal Court, as part of the investigation into Bolsonaro for alleged acts of corruption, money laundering, and currency evasion, ordered that he turn over his passports within 24 hours.
Following this, Bolsonaro posted a video on Instagram stating that he had no intention to leave the country.
However, he later fled the country with his wife and daughters, first to Argentina and then to the United States, heading to Florida.
Bolsonaro fled with the assistance of former Mossad agent Menachem Booky Halevy and on a Baires Fly private jet, a company previously linked to a drug trafficking investigation.

The Argentine government initially stated it had "no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering" the country, but Argentina's immigration ministry admitted a day later to Bolsonaro and his family crossing a land border into Misiones Province and flying out towards Guayaquil in Ecuador.
On October 28, Bolsonaro landed at Miami–Opa Locka Executive Airport, and is expected to receive visas from the Department of State.
After arriving in the US, Bolsonaro published a statement on his X account declaring himself the "true president of Brazil."
The statement featured a modified version of the coat of arms, describing the country as "Estados Unidos do Brazil" (United States of Brazil).
He later deleted the post and republished it with his title changed to "leader of Brazil."

During the campaign, Bolsonaro was associated with the film Dark Horse, a biographical film about his father Jair Bolsonaro starring Jim Caviezel and produced by Eduardo Verástegui, known for producing Sound of Freedom.
Brazilian media described the film as propaganda for the campaign and as a platform for Bolsonarism.

In May 2026, Intercept Brasil reported that Bolsonaro had negotiated funding for Dark Horse with banker Daniel Vorcaro, the former head of Banco Master, who was under investigation in the Banco Master fraud case.

According to the report, Bolsonaro sought up to for the film, and at least R$61 million was allegedly transferred between February and May 2025 through intermediary structures, including Entre Investimentos e Participações and the Texas-based Havengate Development Fund LP, which was described as linked to allies of his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro initially denied the report, but later acknowledged having sought private sponsorship from Vorcaro for what he described as a private film about his father, while denying that he had offered advantages, received money or used public funds.
The production company and Mário Frias denied that funds from Vorcaro or Banco Master had reached the production.

On 15 May 2026, further reporting based on contracts and messages stated that Eduardo Bolsonaro had served as an executive producer on the film with responsibilities for financing strategy, investor materials and fundraising, contradicting his earlier statement that he had merely licensed image rights for the project.

Opposition lawmakers filed a criminal representation with the Prosecutor General's Office and the Federal Police requesting an investigation into Flávio Bolsonaro, Eduardo Bolsonaro, Jair Bolsonaro, Vorcaro and others over the alleged funding arrangements.

Supporters of Lula filed a complaint with the Superior Electoral Court seeking to block the film's release before the election; the court rejected the request, but distributors delayed the theatrical release until 2027, pending the investigations into the film's funding.
After the May 2026 audio recording in which Bolsonaro asked Vorcaro for R$134 million was revealed, further reports and documents were published about the two men's connection.
According to the fact-checking organization Aos Fatos, by September 2026 Bolsonaro had lied at least 43 times about his links to Vorcaro.

sentences.section: Contacts in the days before Vorcaro's arrest
sentences.text: In the days before Vorcaro's first arrest on 17 November 2025, in the context of the Banco Master investigations, Bolsonaro made repeated attempts to contact the banker.

sentences.section: Contacts in the days before Vorcaro's arrest
sentences.text: Records extracted by the Federal Police from Vorcaro's phone and published by Estadão in September 2026 show text messages, unanswered calls and audio exchanges between the two over the four days preceding the police operation.

sentences.section: Contacts in the days before Vorcaro's arrest
sentences.text: On 13 November 2025, Bolsonaro sent a message asking to speak by phone and asking whether Vorcaro could take a call; the banker replied that he would call back later, but no call is recorded that day.

sentences.text: The next day the senator made an unanswered voice call, and the day after, when Vorcaro said he was unavailable, Bolsonaro again sought contact.

sentences.text: On 16 November, the eve of the arrest, Bolsonaro tried again; Vorcaro said he was at church and would call later, and Bolsonaro then declared his support and said he needed guidance on decisions that had to be made.

sentences.section: Contacts in the days before Vorcaro's arrest
sentences.text: Bolsonaro then indicated that his brother Eduardo could travel, offering to help arrange a meeting in the United Arab Emirates, where Vorcaro intended to try to sell Banco Master.

In December 2024, messages later incorporated into the Banco Master investigation recorded discussions about a possible meeting between Vorcaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro and senator Flávio Bolsonaro.
The conversations took place between Vorcaro and the businessman Flávio Carneiro.
In one message, Carneiro asked Vorcaro about his participation in a dinner with his "namesake" and "his father", which investigators associated with Flávio and Jair Bolsonaro respectively.
After initially showing no knowledge of the matter, Vorcaro began to treat it reservedly and asked for discretion, writing: "Man.
Don't tell anyone about this bolso meeting […] This thing destroys me."
It is not clear from the messages whether the dinner actually took place.

On 23 September 2026, the magazine Piauí reported that on 19 January 2025 Bolsonaro had flown from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, to Brasília aboard a Legacy 650 executive jet (registration PP-NLR), in the company of his wife, two daughters and the lawyer and businessman Willer Tomaz de Souza.

At the time, the aircraft was owned jointly through the company Fraction 024 Administração de Bem Próprio S.A., divided into three equal shares: one held by Willer Tomaz, one by the businessman Laércio Cosentino, founder of TOTVS, and a third acquired in late 2024 by Prime You, a company of which Vorcaro was a partner.
Prime You also operated the aircraft through Prime Aviation Táxi Aéreo e Serviços.
The trip took place during the negotiation of the Dark Horse financing.

The investment schedule called for a payment on 20 January 2025, the day after Bolsonaro's return to Brazil; that day the senator contacted Thiago Miranda, identified as an intermediary in the negotiations, asking for speed in the legal review of the investment.
Messages later revealed indicate that Vorcaro pressured the people responsible for the transfers, which ran behind schedule, and the first installment was only transferred in February 2025.

The same aircraft was later identified as the one used in the travels of Supreme Court minister Alexandre de Moraes, whom Bolsonaro had frequently criticized for using the jet before his own trip was reported.

caveats.text: Most of this figure comes from one editor. Editor 18 alone wrote 0.6% of the article, which is 80% of all the text by sanctioned editors. Read it as one editor's contribution, not a pattern across many editors.

This article was chosen by subject (Conservatism and the right), not because Wikipedia marks it as a contentious topic. Wikipedia has no special sanctions area for this subject, so only Wikipedia-wide bans and sockpuppetry findings can count here. Topic bans do not apply.
